title: iter-3 Order.price injection added in dataLayer but exercised by zero tests
description: Iter-3's 1-line patch (actually a ~12-line block at 204-216) adds price-decode injection inside traverseBigVector. The intent — surfacing R5-010's wiring gap — is met at the implementation level: production now sets Order.price for every traversed slice entry. But no test ever enters traverseBigVector. T-014 (networkShape.test.ts:101-110) returns a 'leaf' PoolInner shape where book.asks/book.bids each carry id '0xfakeasks'/'0xfakebids' AND length '0', root_id '0' — and the suix_getDynamicFields stub returns `{ data: [], nextCursor: null, hasNextPage: false }` (line 115). buildPoolInnerState at line 252-255 calls traverseBigVector only when asksId/bidsId is truthy (it is — '0xfakeasks' is truthy), but traverseBigVector immediately returns `[]` at line 168 because `sliceList.data.length === 0`. The new injection code at lines 196-224 is therefore unreachable from any test. Consequently the iter-3 patch could be a no-op, could throw on every order_id, could compute wildly wrong prices, and every test would still pass.
impact: The iter-2 R5-010 high-severity finding (Order.price not wired) is structurally addressed in production code but the closure of the gap is not verified by any test. A future regression that disables the injection (e.g. someone removes the price field assignment during a refactor) would ship green. More urgently — the iter-3 formula `BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n` is uniformly applied to both asks and bids, but ask order_ids have the high bit set (1<<127), so for any real ask the injected price will be ~9.22e18 + actualPrice. There is zero test that constructs a real-shape ask order_id and asserts the injected price equals the encoded price. Production users will see ~9.22e18 prices on every ask card.
recommendation: Tests are sealed for this cycle. File this as a blocking gap for the next cycle: add a dataLayer integration test where the suix_getDynamicFields fixture returns a non-empty slice list AND the sui_getObject for that slice returns a Slice<Order> shape with at least one entry whose order_id is `(1<<127) | (1010<<64) | 1`. Assert the resulting Order.price equals 1010 (not ~9.22e18). The same test should cover a bid with order_id `((U64_MAX - 990) << 64) | 1` and assert price equals 990 (not U64_MAX-990).

title: iter-3 try/catch around BigInt parse silently swallows malformed order_ids — tautology hider
description: The iter-3 patch wraps the price decode in `try { price = Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n); if (!Number.isFinite(price)) price = undefined; } catch { price = undefined; }`. Any malformed order_id (non-numeric string, empty string, '0xdead...' hex with the '0x' prefix preserved, etc.) will fall through silently to `price = undefined`, which then triggers the marketStats fallback decode (which is itself wrong for bids per iter-2 synthesis notes). No test constructs an order_id that fails BigInt parsing; therefore no test would catch a fixture-shape change that quietly disables the entire injection feature. This is exactly the failure mode the R5-010 verification was supposed to lock down.
impact: If a future chain-shape change supplies hex-prefixed order_ids ('0x...') or any non-decimal numeric format, the BigInt('0x...') would actually succeed but if the field shape changes to something like `{value: '12345'}` instead of '12345', the String() coercion would yield '[object Object]' and BigInt would throw — silently caught, price undefined, fallback to broken decodeBidPrice. None of T-005..T-008, T-014, T-019, T-020 would notice.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Document this as a coverage gap: the try/catch should at minimum log via a counter or a console.warn so the test layer can spy on it; or the fallback path should be removed entirely once the data layer is the canonical source.

title: marketStats T-005..T-008 fixtures still construct Orders without `price` — branch coverage of the iter-3 injection path remains zero in compute layer too
description: Iter-3 added the data-layer side of the Order.price injection, but the compute-side branch in computeMarketStats (`o.price !== undefined ? o.price : decodeAskPrice(o.order_id)`, lines 49 and 55 of marketStats.ts) is still exercised exclusively via the fallback-decode arm. The `order(...)` helper (marketStats.test.ts:52-64) returns `{ order_id, quantity, filled_quantity, status }` with no `price` field at all. So even if a future bug rewrote the conditional to `o.price !== undefined ? decodeAskPrice(o.order_id) : o.price` (a swap that produces nonsense in production), every existing T-005..T-008 assertion would still pass — because the fixture path always lands on decodeAskPrice anyway. This is a textbook tautology: the test shape pre-decides which branch runs.
impact: AC1.4 mid-price correctness: the compute layer's preference for injected price over decode is unverified at the unit level. The data-layer R5-001 gap above and this compute-layer gap together mean the entire 'inject price, prefer it' design is verified by zero assertions end-to-end.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Add (next cycle) one fixture row to T-005 where `order(...)` accepts an optional `price` parameter and the assertion is `expect(stats.bestAsk).toBe(<injectedPrice>)` regardless of what decodeAskPrice would have returned for that order_id (e.g. set order_id to a value that decodes to 9999 but inject price=1010, then assert bestAsk===1010).

title: main.tsx production fetch path still uncovered (R5-001 from iter-2 carries forward unchanged)
description: Iter-3 only patched dataLayer.ts. main.tsx is unchanged from iter-2 and still combines manifest fetch + parseManifest + cachedPackageId closure + _origLoadManifest wrapper + createRoot mount with zero tests. T-014 still drives runDataLayer (a sibling entry point); production drives fetchSinglePoolStats per-pool through deps.fetchPoolStats. Wrong manifest URL, missing await, swapped order of wrapper assignment that leaves cachedPackageId as '' at first call, missing root element handling all ship green.
impact: AC1.1/AC1.2 integration glue is unverified. The iter-3 fix did not touch this gap.
recommendation: Restructure main.tsx as a small bootstrap() factory exported and tested with vi.fn() for fetch, OR add an integration smoke test that mounts the full app under jsdom with a fetch spy returning a fixture manifest. Same recommendation as iter-2.

title: 30s sparkline refresh still untested (R5-004 from iter-2 carries forward unchanged)
description: Iter-3 did not address this. App.tsx still has the setInterval(REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=20_000) polling effect; tests still do not use vi.useFakeTimers() or assert fetchPoolStats is called more than once after mount. The interval runs ONLY when state.status === 'ready' (early-return at line 92), so a bug that left state in 'loading' would silently disable polling forever.
impact: AC1.3 freshness has zero executable enforcement. A wrong interval, missing useEffect dep, swapped state check, or missed cleanup leak ships green.
recommendation: Same as iter-2. Tests are sealed. Acknowledge as a gap that should have escalated to E-001 E2E coverage.

title: Vite dev-server middleware still untested (R5-011 from iter-2 carries forward unchanged)
description: Iter-3 did not address this. The Vite middleware that bridges browser-to-localnet.json reads from a hardcoded `~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json` path and has zero tests. A regression in vite.config.ts (wrong path, broken middleware ordering, accidental removal during a config refactor) only surfaces when a developer runs pnpm dev. No CI test catches it.
impact: Same as iter-2. The dev-only bridge between dev server and SPA is not subject to the per-cycle red/green gate.
recommendation: Add a vitest spec that imports the config and verifies the middleware function shape, OR document explicitly that this is dev-only out-of-gate. Same as iter-2.

title: T-014 still uses identical canned response for all sui_getObject calls — Versioned-traversal branch and new iter-3 injection both unexercised (R5-013 carries forward)
description: Iter-3 did not address this; the implications of T-014's spy shape are now sharper. The spy returns the SAME 'leaf' PoolInner payload for every objectId. resolvePoolInnerFields hits the `'book' in fields` early-return branch (dataLayer.ts:117) every time. The Pool→Versioned→PoolInner→getDynamicFields branch (lines 119-152) — which is the production shape per chain-shape.md — is still unexercised by any test. Additionally, the iter-3 traverseBigVector injection at lines 196-220 (the entire reason iter-3 exists) is also unexercised because the spy returns `{data: [], hasNextPage: false}` for suix_getDynamicFields, so traverseBigVector returns [] at line 168 before ever entering the slice loop. T-014's name 'outbound HTTP shape lockdown' is honest — but the test does NOT verify production traversal correctness.
impact: AC1.5's 'no indexer call' is verified, but the chain-direct shape correctness on the production branch remains untested. Combined with R5-001 above, this means iter-3's fix is structurally present in code and exercised by zero tests at every layer.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Acknowledge T-014's scope is URL/method lockdown; add a separate cycle/test for traversal correctness against a captured real-shape fixture (one that returns a Pool wrapper with `inner.fields.id.id`, then a non-empty getDynamicFields response, then a Slice<Order> with real order_ids).

title: types.ts Order.price doc-comment lies about provenance; iter-3 actually decodes from order_id, not from a companion event
description: Order.price's docstring says: 'price is NOT on the chain Order struct; it is injected by the data layer from the corresponding OrderInfo event payload to avoid order_id bit-decode errors on bid orders'. Iter-3's actual implementation (dataLayer.ts:204-216) injects price by bit-decoding the order_id high 64 bits — the exact thing the doc says it is avoiding. No test asserts the provenance of the injected value, so the documentation drift is invisible to the test gate. A reader trusting the doc-comment will assume the injected value reflects an event-side price (real chain price); they will not realize it is an order_id-decode that has the same defects as decodeAskPrice (and a worse defect for bids: it does not invert).
impact: Low at the test-gate layer (no test cares about doc-comments), but feeds back into R5-001/R5-002 above: the fix's documented intent and its implementation diverge, and the test suite cannot detect that.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Either (a) update the docstring to say 'injected by decoding order_id high 64 bits in the data layer' and acknowledge the bid-inversion problem; or (b) actually wire the data layer to OrderInfo events (which would also fix the ask-price ~9.22e18 bug from R5-001).
evidence:
/**
 * Order struct shape from Slice<Order> content — see chain-shape.md Step 4.
 *
 * `price` is NOT on the chain Order struct; it is injected by the data layer
 * from the corresponding OrderInfo event payload to avoid order_id bit-decode
 * errors on bid orders (see chain-shape.md "Critical decoding note").
 */
